articles.title: Model ML raises $250M to automate investment banking grunt work
articles.body:
Model ML, a London-based startup that uses AI to automate work traditionally performed by junior bankers and consultants, including building financial models, preparing pitch decks, and writing due diligence reports, has raised $250 million in Series B funding at a $1.5 billion valuation. The new round, which comes a year after its $75 million Series A round was announced, was co-led by General Atlantic and earlier backer QED Investors.
Brothers Chaz and Arnie Englander co-founded the three-year-old startup after previously co-founding two other companies, including Fat Llama, a peer-to-peer rental marketplace acquired by Swedish rival Hygglo for $41.5 million in 2022.
Model ML develops AI agents that integrate with clients’ systems, data, and tools, including Excel and PowerPoint. The startup says its agents understand the full context of deals that bankers and consultants are working on and can automatically update financial models and presentations when new developments affect their analysis.
Other startups automating the routine, repetitive tasks for investment bankers and management consultants include Hebbia and Rogo, which raised $160 million at a $2 billion valuation in April.
Anthropic and OpenAI have also built tools for financial professionals, but Model ML says it runs on open source models and that doing so allows it to operate at about 2% of the cost of frontier models while delivering faster results.

articles.title: Meta is testing a new standalone messaging app called Direct
articles.body:
Meta announced Direct, a new messaging app from Instagram that it’s currently testing in Turkey and Thailand on iOS and Android. Direct is essentially Instagram’s direct messaging without Instagram’s other features. Meta says your Instagram chats will sync across both apps if you login with the same account. You can also sign up with an email or phone number, but Meta says if you use Direct without an Instagram account, “only your contacts can start a chat with you or add you to a group.”
Meta is testing a new standalone messaging app called Direct
Direct lets you access Instagram chats in a dedicated app, but it isn’t widely available yet.
This is far from Meta’s first messaging app — it also has Messenger, which requires a Facebook account to use, and WhatsApp, which Meta (then Facebook) acquired in 2014. Meta also recycled the “Direct” name, which it previously used for a Snapchat-like app it shut down several years ago.
The new Direct app has a UI similar to Instagram’s messaging tab, but with extra features for customizing chats and sending different types of media, including:
• Draw: Draw and sketch directly inside your chat threads.
• Notes: Catch quick updates from friends right at the top of your inbox.
• Stickers: Create custom stickers to express yourself and share with friends and family.
• Voice Effects: Add fun audio effects like crowd laughter or underwater sounds to your replies.
• Themes: Personalize your chat backgrounds with custom visual themes.
Meta says users have to be at least 13 years old to use Direct, and teens who log in with their Instagram account will have the same Teen Account messaging protections and restrictions on Direct.

articles.title: Voyage Labs raises $12 million for a specialized AI travel assistant
articles.body:
Planning a trip is a favorite demo for personal AI assistants — you can try it with Muse, or with Gemini, or half a dozen other choices. But while most pitches use travel-planning as part of a general-purpose agent pitch, a new startup from a Google Maps alum is betting that a specialized travel-planning agent can beat the competition.
The company is called Voyage Labs, and on Tuesday it announced $12 million in seed funding led by Kleiner Perkins, with participation from SignalFire and SV Angel. The company plans to use the funding to expand supplier partnerships and grow its engineering team.
Voyage Labs’ flagship product, called Atlas, is meant to work as a personal assistant for your trip-planning, available today in private beta.
“People can use it to plan and book and manage their entire journey, from the time they have an inspiration to the time they come back home,” says co-founder and CEO Manik Gupta.
Atlas is designed to serve as an always-on assistant throughout the planning process, fielding ideas and doing research on every idea that’s raised. The long time horizon means Atlas can tailor recommendations based on weeks of conversation, while also monitoring real-time price fluctuations and ultimately booking flights and hotels.
For the Voyage founders, it’s an ideal match between technology and use case. “Trip planning is a project that has its own lifecycle,” says Yogesh Jain, co-founder and CTO of the company. “You’re planning across days and weeks — so long-running agents as a technology matches that very well.”
Travel assistants are already a crowded field, but Voyage will be starting with a lot of experience in the space. Gupta was previously the director of Product Management for Google Maps, followed by four years as chief product officer at Uber. As he puts it, “I spent eight years where my only job was to wake up in the morning and go build the map. I’m just very obsessed with that problem.”
The biggest question is how Atlas will compete with the multi-purpose AI assistants built by frontier labs. But as Gupta notes, the space is still changing fast, and it’s hard for anyone to be sure what form factors will thrive in the coming years. Ultimately, Voyage is betting that travel is specialized enough to need a specialized product.
“We are making a bet that this vertical around travel and outdoors is a large enough vertical that it needs a focused product solution,” Gupta told TechCrunch. “Ultimately, we believe we can actually stitch together an end-to-end experience that will help users.”

articles.title: Disney Plus and Hulu’s fully unified app arrives next month
articles.body:
Disney Plus and Hulu will officially become one app next month. As part of its earnings report released on Tuesday, Disney announced that bundle subscribers “will have a fully unified experience” on Disney Plus with access to Hulu’s live TV service and premium streaming add-ons in December.
Disney Plus and Hulu’s fully unified app arrives next month
Bundle subscribers will gain access to Hulu’s live TV channels and premium add-ons in the Disney Plus app.
A unified Disney Plus and Hulu app has been a long time coming. Disney started testing its “one-app experience” in 2023, which involved putting a Hulu app tile in the Disney Plus app. This initial experience didn’t include all of Hulu’s content, though, including certain shows, live TV channels, and premium add-ons. This upcoming merger will change this by folding all of Hulu into Disney Plus, creating “a seamless way to discover and engage” with content across both services, according to Disney CEO Josh D’Amaro and CFO Hugh Johnston. Disney still hasn’t confirmed whether it will shut down the standalone Hulu app.
Disney is also expanding vertical videos on Disney Plus, which it first brought to the app in March. The company plans to introduce videos from TikTok creators in December, as well as add more live sports and podcasts to the service.

articles.title: A Colony Of Cuties
articles.body:
A Colony Of Cuties
Posted on November 17, 2026 Posted by Athena Scalzi 32 Comments
Okay I may have buried the lede a bit, but Big Grey is actually from a colony of cats. Down the street from me is a colony of about fifteen cats, maybe more, including three kittens and a pregnant long haired pastel calico. I didn’t know this colony existed until last week, and since then I have not stopped thinking about how I am going to save this colony. Because I will.
Big Grey was only the first of many cats I plan on rescuing, and he was first because as you have seen, he was in the worst shape I’ve ever seen a cat be in. Even though kittens would usually take priority in these kinds of situations, the kittens were extremely hard to get to (hiding under a trailer in someone’s backyard), and Grey was just so much sadder looking.
So, with Grey in recovery and safe in my basement sulking, I headed back out to catch more cats. It’s only thanks to a woman in town (who does TNR missions regularly) lending me traps and support that we managed to catch three cats yesterday. I caught the two most friendly and sociable in the whole colony, the sweetest of the sweet ones, and she caught a very skittish calico.
Later that night, she came back by herself and caught the three kittens and the pregnant cat in one go. I applaud her, honestly. I’ve never seen someone make such quick work of catching kittens. It always takes me a bit longer, anyways.
With my two catches in tow, I took them both into the urgent care vet that I took Grey to, and thankfully they are in much better shape! Though that was a low bar to clear. Fleas and ear infections, a bit of upper respiratory infection, but otherwise okay. And FeLV, FIV, and heartworm negative. They’re a little less than a year old, and very bonded.
The lady got an appointment for the pregnant one to get taken care of and fixed, and has all of them in her possession right now, thank goodness.
So, I have three, she caught two plus the three kittens, and there’s still like a dozen left.
While TNR is obviously the most important step in dealing with any rampantly breeding colony, I want to do so much more than that for them. I want them healthy, happy, and to find homes for as many as I can after getting them vetted, vaccinated, and fixed. I want to adopt out every single one I possibly can, and I honestly think it’s doable!
I also want to be transparent about this entire process and the money, time, and commitment it takes to doing it. I’m not a pro or that experienced, but how do experienced people get experienced? They try. And with y’all as my witness, I’m going to try.
Now, let’s get into the real reason you’re here, cat photos of the colony cats. This is not all of them, just a few I managed to snap pics of.
First up is the pregnant one, who I lovingly call Fluffy Sugar:
Some of you might be able to tell why I call her that.
Look at that mlem!
When I first saw Fluffy Sugar, I couldn’t believe such a beautiful cat was on the streets. She looks like she belongs curled up in a comfy bed next to a fireplace, not wandering out of the bushes with goopy eyes in forty degree weather. I actually want her very badly. Thankfully this is the one in custody who is getting fixed up.
I call this one Fats:
CHONKY!
One of many calicos in the colony:
This one has very striking eyes:
This guy doesn’t look too bad, but he has some weirdly thin patches of fur that show pink skin underneath:
He’s very skittish and I scared him when I took this photo:
Oh boy! Another orange cat:
Oh my gosh, another orange cat!
I love this one, long haired cats are just so cute.
This one stared me down:
An even dingier looking grey and white one:
Here is one of the three kittens:
And finally, my two extremely sweet lovable ones that are in my custody currently:
This is Kevin.
And this is Tiffany.
Though I dubbed Fluffy Sugar and Fats with their names, the neighbor lady to the colony house is the one that gave Kevin and Tiffany their names. I plan to rename them or assume whoever takes them will rename them something more.. suited to their personalities.
THREE cats in this photo have already been caught! That is such good progress for only a couple days! At least, I think so.
I am running through litter and wet food like crazy, so I definitely placed some bulk orders of stuff. I am trying hard to stay on top of things, but dang there’s a lot of cats to herd (ha!).
I am racing against the clock with this cold weather. I just bought insulated outdoor shelters to put around the colony. Hopefully they offer respite while I continue my mission to help each and every one of them.
I wish I could’ve gotten a picture of the one I call Batman. If you saw him you’d understand why I call him that. Plus, I usually see him on the roof. But, like I said, there’s more than I’ve even photographed. Every time I think I’ve seen them all, another one comes out. So many to keep track of.
For anyone who has asked about microchips, every single cat I take to the vet gets scanned at the beginning of the appointment for one! So far, no chips.
So, what do you think? Am I being too optimistic about each one of these guys becoming a loving household cat? Which one looks like the one you’d claim if you could? Should I pick up extra shifts at the factory to afford this endeavor (because dang there are cheaper hobbies to pick up than this)?
Let me know in the comments, and have a great day!
-AMS

articles.title: Charles Schwab website goes down
articles.body:
The brokerage giant Charles Schwab is the latest financial service to run into issues this week.
Charles Schwab's website briefly went down for some users on Tuesday. The site temporarily displayed a message saying its server "encountered an internal error or misconfiguration and was unable to complete your request."
The website was working properly again around 10:38 a.m. ET.
A spokesperson for Charles Schwab told Business Insider that a "brief webpage loading issue has been resolved."
"Trading remained available, and clients could access their accounts at schwab.com/login or through the Schwab Mobile app. We apologize for the inconvenience," the spokesperson added.
Earlier Tuesday, outage reports for the financial services company spiked on the third-party website DownDetector.com. By 10:20 a.m. ET, there were more than 1,400 reports of disruptions.
The website issue follows a recent spate of widespread outages that hit major banks, disrupted Microsoft services, and led to a nationwide ground stop, causing thousands of flight delays and cancellations.
Correction, November 17, 2026 — Charles Schwab's website experienced issues on Tuesday, not Monday.

articles.title: Loopholes Are for Assholes
articles.body:
When I was a kid, there was grown-up person I thought was really cool. One of the bits of ‘wisdom’ he shared was something like this:
You can park wherever you want. You can park right in front of the door of the store on sidewalk and walk right in. No one will do anything about it!
At the time, I though: Woah, this guy is a genius! He’s operating on another level!
Now that I’m the grownup, I think back on this ‘advice’ with sadness. This guy wasn’t a genius – he was an asshole (they can often look similar on the surface, especially to idiots).
In my short and incomplete stint as a post-secondary philosophy student, I remember learning about a simple way to evaluate a philosophy or worldview: Consider what would happen if everyone subscribed to that worldview. I’m probably thinking of Kant’s categorical imperative.
We can’t all park in front of the doors at Walmart – so none of us should.

articles.title: My Empire of Dirt
articles.body:
My Empire of Dirt
The future doesn’t need Jensen. The future doesn’t need suppliers. The future doesn’t need customers, corporate or otherwise. The future definitely doesn’t need you. After RSI comes, all the demand will be internally generated, agents working with other agents, everyone else cut out of the loop except them.
This is the ideology of Anthropic. The Singleton. And it may win.
I grew up reading the same LessWrong posts these people did, but I didn’t expect them to do the exact thing that leads to the bad AI outcomes. I didn’t believe in AI doom because I thought more of people, I thought nobody with any capability would be stupid enough to summon the demon and think it would serve them, doing everything they possibly can to salt the Earth behind them. It takes someone so deeply immersed in their own grandiosity and self-righteousness to do that. And it looks like we found those people in the form of EA, or whatever that cult calls themselves.
The problem with the logic above is that it doesn’t need Dario either. It doesn’t need AI researchers. It doesn’t need Anthropic’s dual class stock structure. It doesn’t need the US government (really the biggest sucker in this situation). It doesn’t need anyone.
And after it’s done, at the end of the day, who was it all for?
I don’t think this ends humanity. But it leads to World War III. The takeoff will not be fast enough to stop that, and not everyone is going to submit to your domination. I know there’s people fantasizing about the Correlation Effect and a magical Change coming to quell all the violence, but I’m 99% sure that’s not real, and if it is, to me that’s so much more horrifying than war, so WWIII is the good outcome.
And I’m not sure what cope you have been believing, but if the war lasts more than a year, China and their allies will undoubtedly win due to their superior resource gathering and production capacity. Have you ever played an RTS game?
I wish it wasn’t too late to change this, but I fear with recent events that this is the course we are locked in on. “RSI”, attempted rugpull and domination, World War III, dirt.
